evidence.dominant_driver: Qatar is trying to broker a short-term US-Iran agreement to restart negotiations, but says a deal is hard to achieve and any initial accord would only open broader talks.

market_expectations.expected_value: Markets entered Asia with substantial de-escalation optimism already priced after oil's multi-day drop; a difficult negotiation path challenges, but does not eliminate, that assumption.
market_expectations.distribution_notes: No final deal is expected immediately; the relevant near-term outcome is a framework to restart negotiations.

absorption.reason: The warning arrived after several sessions of diplomacy-driven oil declines and a strong US equity rally. By decision time oil had only modestly rebounded and Asian equities remained risk-on.

observations.VIX: risk-on carryover; exact fresh value unavailable
observations.interpretation: Oil/gold show a small geopolitical-premium rebuild, but equities and rates do not confirm a broad risk-off move.

evidence.decision_notes: Residual forecast made ~101 minutes after Forex Factory posting. This is continuation of the US-Iran diplomacy cluster, not a fresh independent war shock. Leakage-safe M2 profile materially supports low-confidence MIXED at 15m/1h and warns against 1h directional confidence 5-6.

regimes.risk: Asian equities risk-on after prior US rally; diplomacy hopes remain priced
regimes.energy: oil stabilizing/rebounding after sharp multi-day decline
regimes.rates: Treasury yields eased in prior session
regimes.geopolitics: Qatar says only a short-term agreement to restart talks is plausible and path remains fraught

immediate.rationale: The article is roughly 100 minutes old; gold is only edging higher and the dollar remains firm, so residual safe-haven continuation is weak.

next_session.rationale: The outcome remains binary: even a limited agreement to restart negotiations could quickly unwind renewed safe-haven demand.

15m.rationale: The article is roughly 100 minutes old; gold is only edging higher and the dollar remains firm, so residual safe-haven continuation is weak.

1h.rationale: Oil is rebounding slightly and diplomacy looks difficult, but falling yields and a firm dollar pull gold in opposite directions.

4h.rationale: If the Qatar warning reduces confidence in a near-term diplomatic breakthrough, some geopolitical premium can rebuild in gold.

next_session.rationale: The outcome remains binary: even a limited agreement to restart negotiations could quickly unwind renewed safe-haven demand.

predictions.mechanism: Harder diplomacy preserves geopolitical safe-haven demand, while a firm dollar offsets part of that support.
predictions.invalidation: A confirmed short-term US-Iran framework or renewed sharp oil decline would invalidate the 4h upside view.
predictions.counter_case: Qatar may still secure a framework to restart negotiations; if oil falls again and the dollar stays firm, gold can resume lower.

immediate.rationale: US cash is closed and Asian risk appetite remains firm; no clean immediate equity risk-off confirmation exists.

next_session.rationale: If no short-term framework emerges and oil extends its rebound, geopolitical/inflation risk can weigh on the next US cash session.

15m.rationale: US cash is closed and Asian risk appetite remains firm; no clean immediate equity risk-off confirmation exists.

1h.rationale: A modest oil rebound is negative, but markets still price a meaningful chance of talks and Asian equities remain strong.

4h.rationale: The Qatar comments are cautionary rather than a breakdown of diplomacy, limiting a directional residual call.

next_session.rationale: If no short-term framework emerges and oil extends its rebound, geopolitical/inflation risk can weigh on the next US cash session.

predictions.mechanism: Failure of diplomacy can rebuild oil/inflation and geopolitical tail risk for US equities.
predictions.invalidation: A confirmed negotiation framework plus renewed oil weakness would invalidate the next-session downside view.
predictions.counter_case: The comments explicitly describe ongoing mediation toward restarting talks, while falling oil and AI momentum can keep risk appetite strong.
